question: Which exact REDMI Watch 6 3.100.043 entry points back battery state, wake locks, screen state/wake, manual brightness, vibration, system properties, Bluetooth adapter and MiWear link state, heap, file and time services for the Supervisor platform hooks, and do their ABIs match what the Supervisor calls?
prototype_hypothesis: Stock PowerManager/MiWearScreen/property/Bluetooth-client/system_state APIs and the NuttX VFS/clock/heap entries are ordinary AAPCS Thumb functions called from the UI owner thread, with the same arguments as the Band 10 Pro 3.101.043 records; file entries are libc style (-1 and errno through errno_location 0xc4f793c, which the 0x1c-resident VFS code reaches through the thunk 0x1c168478).
callsite_evidence: wakelock_acquire calls screen_session_start(session, 1) and screen_turn_on("wakelock", 26); wakelock_release calls screen_get_state() and screen_session_stop(session).
screen_init 0xca69ad4 reads persist.screen.brightness_value through property_get_int32 (default 123); the stock setter 0xca68a4c clamps to 31..255.
The miwear Bluetooth init 0xca3f3d8 creates the instance returned by bt_adapter_get_instance and compares bt_adapter_get_state with 4 (on).
update_from_bt_state 0xc931030 writes system_state byte +1 = 2 for a MiWear connection, else 1.
Stock code fsyncs then closes a descriptor (0x1c05bae0 -> 0x1c159e88, 0x1c154d9c).
control_flow_evidence: power_battery_ready = 0xca61d20 (ported 0x1c15f8cc): Returns byte 0x3c4963b8 ? byte 0x3c4963b9 : 0. set_battery_state_from_topic_data (inlined in uv_topic_battery_state_cb 0xca61388) sets 0x3c4963b8 with 'battery charging state is ready' and 0x3c4963b9 with 'battery level is ready'. The ported address has no code reference.
power_battery_charging = 0xca61d58 (ported 0xca195d4): Returns byte 0x3c4963bc, written as (topic state == 1) by the battery_state callback.

power_battery_level = 0xca61d70 (ported 0xca61d70): Returns the u32 at 0x3c4963c0, written by the callback only for level <= 100. 0xca61d3c next to it copies 8 bytes {charging, level} (a snapshot-style getter); the three getters are used.

wakelock_create = 0xca61e9c (ported 0xca61e9c): __func__ 'wakelock_create' (0x3c3514b8); accepts (uint16)level 6 or 26 else logs 'invalid levelAndFlags', calloc(1,36), tag at +8, screen session from screen_session_create("wakelock") at +32, links into the wakelock list 0x3c496304, returns NULL on allocation failure.
wakelock_acquire = 0xca61ffc (ported 0xca61ffc): Count at +20; the first acquire calls screen_session_start(session, 1) and, when the turn-on flag at +14 is set, screen_turn_on("wakelock", 26).
wakelock_release = 0xca620c4 (ported 0xca620c4): Count at +20; the last release calls screen_session_stop(session), after the screen_get_state() == 2 dimmer path.
screen_get_state = 0xca68fac (ported 0xca68fac): Returns 2 while the on-counter 0x3c4969bc > 0, else the state byte 0x3c4969c4; wakelock_release compares the result with 2.

screen_turn_on = 0xca69200 (ported 0x1c00c494): __func__ 'screen_turn_on' with 'system is shutting, refuse to turn on screen, tag=%s'; (tag, source) forwarded to the turn-on worker 0xca67cf0. The ported address is the Bluetooth client send/receive helper used by every 0x1c008xxx adapter call.
screen_session_create = 0xca68abc (ported 0xca68abc): __func__ 'screen_session_create'; calloc(1,32), tag at +8, +12/+24 = -1, idle list 0x3c4968d8.

screen_session_start = 0xca68bd8 (ported 0xca68bd8): __func__ 'screen_session_start', log 'tag=%s, handle=%p, auto_stop=%s'; auto_stop byte at +28, moves the session to the active list 0x3c4968e0 and re-arbitrates.
screen_session_stop = 0xca68c6c (ported 0xca68c6c): __func__ 'screen_session_stop'; moves an active session back to the idle list and re-arbitrates.
screen_session_set_auto_brightness = 0xca68e28 (ported 0xca68e28): __func__ 'screen_session_set_auto_brightness'; status byte at +20, status string table 0x3c3541c8 index 1 ENABLED, 2 DISABLED.

screen_session_set_brightness_value = 0xca68e8c (ported 0xca68e8c): __func__ 'screen_session_set_brightness_value'; int value at +24. The stock persist.screen.brightness_value setter 0xca68a4c clamps to 31..255.
screen_session_restore_default = 0xca68f38 (ported 0xca68f38): __func__ 'screen_session_restore_default'; +12/+24 = -1, +16/+20 = 0, re-arbitrates while active.

property_get = 0xcb93434 (ported 0xc78c878): Key length <= 127, reads up to 255 bytes and returns the length when NUL terminated; otherwise copies the default and returns its length, or -22 when value or default is NULL. The ported address is an LVGL label text helper.

property_get_int32 = 0xcb93a24 (ported 0x36a784): property_get(key, buf[256], NULL), strtol with errno and end-pointer check, else default. screen_init 0xca69ad4 reads persist.screen.auto_brightness (default 1) and persist.screen.brightness_value (default 123) through it. The ported address is a ROM ADC routine.

bt_adapter_get_instance = 0xca3f474 (ported 0xca3f474): Returns the global 0x3c4942b0; the miwear Bluetooth init 0xca3f3d8 stores bluetooth_create_instance() (XIP veneer 0xc8be8c0 -> 0x1c001b54) there and calls bt_adapter_get_state on it; headset AG init logs 'bt_ins is NULL' when it returns NULL.

bt_adapter_get_state = 0x1c008720 (ported 0x1c0087a4): Client command 27: NULL instance or transport failure -> 0, else reply byte +4. Callers: bttool 'Adapter State: %d', the btclient test, and the miwear Bluetooth init through veneer 0xc8beb28, which compares the result with 4 (on). The ported address is command 32 (returns 1 on failure) and has no callers. Same entry as private_abi.bt_adapter_get_state_exact.

system_get_state = 0xc931d04 (ported 0x1c0bf164): 17-way switch over the state id; zeroes out[0..1], stores the state byte, returns out. Ids 0..9 and 14..16 log 'Please call system_init_state first.' and spin forever when the pointer 0x3c47a328 is NULL. The ported address is an LVGL routine.

system_state = 0x3c47a328 (ported none): system_init_state 0xc931904 mallocs 20 bytes and stores the pointer here; update_from_bt_state 0xc931030 writes byte +1 = 2 (MiWear connected) or 1 and byte +2 = ACL flag + 1.
heap_malloc = 0xc50b2a0 (ported 0xc50b2a0): mm_malloc over the default heap descriptor dword_3C3D4F10[3043]; errno ENOMEM and NULL on failure. system_init_state allocates its state with it.
heap_free = 0xc50b25c (ported 0xc50b25c): Forwards (heap, ptr) to the mm free body; same entry as mm_free_default. Prototype set to void(void *).

lseek = 0x1c157b90 (ported 0xc6b9c80): vfs/fs_lseek.c assert; fs_getfilep 0x1c154700, inode seek op or SEEK_SET/SEEK_CUR on f_pos (+8 int64, SEEK_END without an op is ENOSYS), fs_putfilep, returns f_pos in R0:R1 and -1/-1 with errno. Offset in R2:R3, whence on the stack, matching int64_t(int, int64_t, int). The ported address is an unrelated release routine.
mkdir = 0x1c157c5c (ported 0x1c157c5c): vfs/fs_mkdir.c assert; mode &= ~umask, EEXIST for an existing node, mountpoint mkdir op (+84) or pseudo-directory reserve, -1 with errno.

fsync = 0x1c159e88 (ported 0x1c159e88): fs_getfilep, mountpoint sync op (+36) or the driver ioctl result clamped to 0, EINVAL without an op, fs_putfilep, -1 with errno. Stock code 0x1c05bae0 calls it right before close 0x1c154d9c.
rmdir = 0x1c158b08 (ported 0x1c158b08): vfs/fs_rmdir.c assert; mountpoint rmdir op (+88); a pseudo node with ops is ENOTDIR, one with children ENOTEMPTY; -1 with errno.

clock_gettime = 0xc4c205c (ported 0xc4c6be0): clock/clock_gettime.c assert on a NULL timespec; clock ids 1 and 4 read the system timespec, 0 adds the base time 0x3c3d4080, other ids EINVAL; stores tv_sec as int64 at +0 (STRD) and tv_nsec as int32 at +8, so the p65 timespec is {int64 sec, int32 nsec} padded to 16 bytes. The ported address is a semaphore wait.

lv_timer_create = 0xc7414d8 (ported 0xc8bcc98): LVGL v9 lv_timer_create(cb, period, user_data): lv_ll_ins_head on the timer list 0x3c4500b4 walked by lv_timer_handler 0xc7412ec; period +0, last_run = lv_tick_get (0xc7828d8) +4, cb +8, user_data +12, repeat_count -1 +16, paused cleared / auto_delete set at +20. 0xc74154c next to it is lv_timer_delete. The ported address is a veneer to an unrelated LVGL routine 0x1c129c9c.

stat = 0x1c1595a4 (ported 0x1c1572b4): vfs/fs_stat.c: stat 0x1c1595a4 (inode_stat resolve 1, errno), lstat 0x1c15967c, nx_stat 0x1c1594f8. inode_stat 0x1c159300 clears a 96-byte struct stat: st_mode +8, st_size int64 +24; file_fchstat 0x1c1572b4 (the ported address) places st_atim/st_mtim/st_ctim as 16-byte timespecs at +32/+48/+64. ABI MISMATCH: the Supervisor stat hook assumes the 104-byte Band 10 Pro layout (st_size +32, st_mtim.tv_sec +72). Left CANDIDATE.

vibrator_hal_transact = none (ported 0x1c14204c): No vibratord HAL client exists on p65. Vibration goes through miwear_vibrator_run 0xca737a8 (copies a 12-byte block; type byte +0 must be a preset effect 1..25, priority byte +8; returns an id or -2/-3/-4/-5) and miwear_vibrator_cancel 0xca738b0(id); the player 0xc92b578 only plays preset effect tables. Neither Supervisor path (132-byte HAL message, Band 11 20-byte waveform block) fits. The ported address is an LVGL layout routine. Left CANDIDATE without an address.

exact 3.100.043 IDB vela_ap.bin.i64 (PowerManager, MiWearScreen, property library, Bluetooth client, system_state, NuttX VFS/clock/heap and LVGL timer review); the Band 10 Pro 3.101.043 IDB could not be opened, so its record notes and EVID-PLATFORM-HW-1043-001 were the reference.
ownership_analysis: wakelock and screen session objects are heap objects owned by the creator; the Supervisor creates a bounded set once and never destroys them. Tag strings passed to create calls must outlive the objects. system_state is read-only. Heap allocations come from the stock default heap (PSRAM).
unsafe_assumptions: Device NOT_PROBED: no Mirage or device run backs any entry in this bundle.
No device probe: argument registers, blocking behavior and thread affinity are inferred from decompilation only.
bt_adapter_get_state is a Bluetooth client IPC round trip and blocks the caller.
Brightness override relies on session arbitration; stock UI may overwrite it when the user changes brightness.
recommended_probe: Mirage or device: query battery, toggle a Canopus wakelock with the screen idle, set brightness to 20% and 100% and restore, read the Bluetooth adapter and MiWear link state, mkdir/rmdir/lseek/fsync a test path, read CLOCK_MONOTONIC twice.

artifacts.role: exact REDMI Watch 6 3.100.043 firmware image reviewed
